_what: How this Mac trusts an update or a download list (computer/signed-manifest.mjs): a manifest is JSON text that came with a detached Ed25519 signature, and counts only when one of the publisher keys below verifies it. `keys` are the publishers this Mac trusts: { id, public_key } (the 32 raw bytes, base64), with an optional `retired_at` after which that key no longer counts. A manifest holds `entries`: { version, channel?, url, size, blake3 } (blake3 is the 64 hex characters of the artifact). With none of the trusted keys listed, nothing is trusted. The check stops at the first fact that fails.

words.no_keys: This Mac trusts no update publisher, so the list was not used.
words.unsigned: The list has no signature, so it was not used.
words.bad_signature: The list's signature does not match any publisher this Mac trusts, so it was not used.
words.not_json: The signed list is not readable.
words.no_newer: Nothing newer than {current} is listed for {channel}.
words.downgrade: {version} is older than {current}; this Mac does not go back.
words.wrong_artifact: The downloaded file does not match the size and hash the signed list names, so it was not used.
